beginner.title: Beginner Roadmap
beginner.description: Zero to comfortable: navigate the filesystem, manage files, read documentation, and run your first scripts.

steps.title: Find your way around
steps.body: Learn where you are and how to move. These four commands are the foundation of everything else.

steps.title: Create and organize
steps.body: Make files and directories, copy and move them around.

steps.title: Read files and search text
steps.body: View file contents and find the lines you need.

steps.title: Delete carefully
steps.body: Remove files and directories — and learn why rm deserves respect.

steps.title: Get help and go faster
steps.body: Use the manual, history, and tab completion effectively.

steps.title: Permissions first contact
steps.body: Understand rwx and make your scripts executable.

intermediate.title: Intermediate Roadmap
intermediate.description: From comfortable to capable: administer users and services, master text pipelines, and manage disks.

steps.title: Text processing power
steps.body: Build pipelines that answer real questions about logs and data.

steps.title: Users and privileges
steps.body: Create accounts, manage groups, and use sudo correctly.

steps.title: Processes and monitoring
steps.body: Find, inspect, and control running programs.

steps.title: Services with systemd
steps.body: Start, stop, enable, and diagnose services — the core of server work.

steps.title: Disks and storage
steps.body: Partition, format, mount, and monitor storage.

steps.title: Networking basics
steps.body: Check addresses, routes, ports, and connectivity.

advanced.title: Advanced Roadmap
advanced.description: From capable to expert: security hardening, kernel internals, containers from first principles, and deep troubleshooting.

steps.title: Security and firewalls
steps.body: Harden SSH, manage firewalls, and encrypt data.

steps.title: Advanced permissions
steps.body: Go beyond rwx: special bits, ACLs, and umask strategy.

steps.title: Deep troubleshooting
steps.body: Trace system calls, open files, and kernel events.

steps.title: Kernel and boot
steps.body: Manage modules, kernel parameters, and the boot process.

steps.title: Containers from first principles
steps.body: Understand what Docker does by using namespaces directly.

steps.title: Performance engineering
steps.body: Priorities, affinity, and resource limits in production.
